Reproduce that structure and that cutting rhythm, and replace everything inside it with this product and this room. Shot one, macro inside the beam: the perforated grille filling the frame, light raking across the aluminium, dust lifting off the grille as a low bass pulse moves it. Shot three, extreme macro: the light travelling along the brushed yoke and the stitched leather cushion, the cushion compressing once. Shot four, low hero: the light narrowing to a sliver across the aluminium ring, the hall falling almost dark with one specular left. No people anywhere, no text or logos. nodes.title: Note: Reference Video as Shot Template
widgets_values:
**Input Assets**

- [kling4_anc_headphones.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_anc_headphones.png) — the product to shoot
- [kling4_monolith_hall.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_monolith_hall.png) — the place it is shot in
- [kling4_refvideo_spot.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_refvideo_spot.mp4) — a reference clip whose shot structure is reproduced

## Shot the reference, not the subject

`@Video1` carries the structure: how many shots, what each one frames, how the camera behaves and roughly when the cuts fall. Images carry the subject and the room. That split is what makes this the useful way to work — a clip that already looks right becomes a template you re-shoot with your own product, your own set and your own character.

What actually transfers, measured on this template: four shots in, four shots out, same order of shot types (product macro, wide of the space, detail macro, low hero), and cut points within about a quarter second of the reference rather than frame-exact. Treat the timing as a rhythm, not a timecode.

What does *not* stay separated is camera from action. A reference clip containing a punch produced a punch in the output even with an explicit `never copy its content` instruction; a reference that contains only product and camera behaviour leaked nothing. So pick a reference whose *actions* you are happy to inherit, not just whose camera you like.

Keep the reference around five seconds and the same duration as the target so the structure maps one to one. Up to five reference videos can be connected (`@Video1…@Video5`); mix them only when each contributes a different thing.

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_Frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_Frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)
